text:
Appendix 5: Requirements for accrediting bodies
This section explains the requirements for accrediting bodies, including MCA and DESNZ audits every 3 years, the process for addressing any deficiencies, and arrangements for withdrawal from the scheme.
Auditing of accrediting bodies by MCA and DESNZ
The Memorandum of Agreement (MoA) between Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ), the Maritime Coastguard Agency (MCA) and the accrediting body requires the accrediting body’s activities to be audited every 3 years. Audits are based on the Standard and the relevant MoA. The MCA and DESNZ will provide supporting documentation before the audit, including details of the audit process and follow-up activity.
If the MCA or Offshore Petroleum Regulator for Environment and Decommissioning (OPRED) identifies deficiencies during an audit, these will be communicated to the accrediting body and a timescale for remediation will be agreed. Depending on the nature of the deficiency, the MCA or OPRED may take action to ensure the deficiency is not reflected in the activities of Oil Spill Response Organisations’ (OSROs’) accredited by that body.
If an accrediting body withdraws from the scheme and there are no outstanding issues, OSROs accredited by that body will remain accredited until the end of their accreditation period.
Requirements for accrediting bodies
Bodies wishing to provide accreditation services must meet the following requirements:
- there must be no conflict of interest between the accrediting body and the OSRO industry, demonstrated to the satisfaction of the MCA and DESNZ
- the accrediting body must submit its proposed accreditation scheme to the MCA and DESNZ for approval
- the accreditation scheme must comply with the framework set out in the Standard
- MCA and DESNZ approval will be formalised through a Memorandum of Agreement (MoA)
- accreditation fees must be agreed with the MCA and DESNZ
- the accrediting body must hold a recognised and current quality management system, for example ISO 9001
- auditors must be approved by the MCA and DESNZ and have appropriate knowledge and experience of the marine oil spill response industry
- the accrediting body must report all accreditations and the requirements met by OSROs as part of annual returns
- the accrediting body must have a complaints procedure
- the accrediting body must report on general industry trends relating to OSROs, including: 
  - incidents involving UK OSROs
  - major organisational developments, such as changes in specialisms and capability
OSRO documentation retention
Accrediting bodies should retain copies of key documents from accredited OSROs and review them annually alongside the OSRO annual return. This helps identify changes that could affect service provision.
Documents retained should include, but are not limited to:
- client risk profiles
- capability matrices
- significant sub-contractual documentation
Continuous professional development
Auditors working for accrediting bodies are expected to maintain current knowledge of oil spill response through continuous professional development (CPD).
CPD may include:
- deployment to incidents
- participation in exercises
- attendance at conferences
- relevant training courses
- other suitable activities
CPD activities should be recorded and evidence may be requested by the MCA or DESNZ during audits.
